review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Many people believe that advertising plays a key role in economic developments, while others concern it could adversely affect the society. From my perspective, there are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, advertising bring various undeniable economic benefits. Initially, creative content with appealing visual effects might significantly stimulate consumer. Consequently, the spending power would be increased, leading to the encouragement of production throughout the whole country. Hence, more there would be more opportunities for people who are unemployed and greater state revenues through taxation. Moreover, more different occupations in the field of marketing, media and design are created, making it an important driver of economic activity.

On the other hand, some people argued that advertising has negative social consequences. Firstly, advertising constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards or luxury possessions which foster dissatisfaction among viewers. A realistic example is that young people, in particular, feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook, consequently resulting in frustration when they cannot afford them. To a further extent, advertising promote materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run.
Overall, while both views are valid to some certain extent. Although advertising contribute to social dissatisfaction, it also plays a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: Many people believe that advertising plays a key role in economic development, whereas others are concerned that it could adversely affect society. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content with appealing visual effects can significantly stimulate consumer demand. Consequently, spending power increases, encouraging production throughout the country. Hence, more employment opportunities are created and state revenues increase through taxation. For example, online retailers can use advertising campaigns to reach more customers and expand the digital market. Furthermore, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media, and design, making it an important driver of economic activity.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. It constantly shows images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards, and luxury possessions, which foster dissatisfaction among viewers. Young people in particular may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook, resulting in frustration when they cannot afford them. In the long run, advertising promotes materialistic values and a money-driven culture.
In conclusion, I believe both views are valid to a certain extent. Although advertising contributes to social dissatisfaction, it also plays a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: It is argued that people's lives nowadays are largely influenced by the news media; personally, I believe that although news media contains several negative information, its positive development is far more effective.

Granted, the dissemination of news media has many effects on people. Initially, due to the wide spread access to smartphones and the Internet, people are allowed to follow the news instantly, even wherever and whenever they are, which become a regular part of their routine. Moreover, the intense competition among news outlets, in order to gain attention, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content, then presenting it in a highly sensationalized manner along with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals. As a consequence, the overall impact of news on public opinion is significantly reinforced.

However, I strongly concur that the coverage of news media brings both pros and cons. Admittedly, news media, in particular, does have noticeable disadvantages. Exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news would further overwhelm people, resulting in feeling overly anxious and helplessness, even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, news coverage would warn the public to existing and looming problems in society, say, crime, natural disasters or political corruption. Hence, individuals are better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, handling risks in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, the influence of news media on current society is significant yet I am firmly convinced that despite its negative effects, the positive sides are way more pronounced.

paragraphs: It is argued that schools should reward students with the best results in academic performance, whereas others concur students who gradually improve are more desirable. Personally, I agree that both those kind of students should be rewarded.

Admittedly, it is fundamental that school should reward the out-performing students. Students, who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, deserve their praises and privileges. Hence, this may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, propeling them towards overall academic improvements. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life where only the most astonishing individuals are rewarded. As a consequent, students are used to this reality and continue to thrive in the face of fierce competition, which eventually enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students with improving academic performance should also received incentive rewards from school. Since only a few smart students can come first and achieve the rewards, it causes others to think that their effort is futile being unable to surpass those outstanding individuals makes students prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, gradually losing the incentive to study. Thus, emphasizing improvement not only encourages students to be diligent in their studies but also helps student to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Furthermore, students would have the constant desire to outdo themselves, even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all other.
In conclusion, although talented students are believed to receive academic rewards, it is undoubtedly important to incentivize students who perform better at school.

paragraphs: It is argued that schools should reward students with the best results in academic performance, whereas others believe that students who gradually improve are more deserving of rewards. Personally, I agree that both kinds of students should be rewarded.

Admittedly, it is fundamental that schools reward the high-achieving students. Initially, students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies deserve their praises and privileges. Hence, this recognition may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, propelling them towards overall academic improvements. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life where only the highest-achieving individuals are rewarded. As a consequence, students become used to this reality and continue to thrive in the face of fierce competition, which can eventually enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students with improving academic performance should also receive rewards from school. First, since only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, this exclusive reward system may cause others to think that their effort is futile. This is because they may feel unable to surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasizing improvement not only encourages students to be diligent in their studies but also helps students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Students may also develop a constant desire to outdo themselves, which may benefit them more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, although rewarding students with outstanding academic results is justified, it is undoubtedly important to incentivize students who show improvement at school.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: In some particular countries, children are being taught face-to-face with their parents rather than going to school. Personally, I believed that the disadvantages are far more significant than the advantages that homeschooling provides.

It is argued that homeschooling does have several benefits for both parents and children. Firstly, as no school fees are required, it allows parents to save money and avoid financial problems at school. Moreover, when children are educated at home, they are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which cause emotional and mental disorders. Also, parents can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches while teaching their children at home by themselves, often not being the case in traditional schooling because of the large class size.

However, those advantages of homeschooling are not practically positive. Initially, this educational approach do not actually save money as parents need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipment and tutors. Subsequently, one parents need to be cut off to cater for their child's needs. Furthermore, most parents are not well-versed in all school subjects, leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately academic problems. Last but not least, even the social problems that children are faced with at school, say, bullying or having romantic feelings for others, actually prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, although the merits of homeschooling are noticeable, I am of convinced that its demerits is far more noticeable.
review.overall: Em hoàn thành bốn đoạn, nêu rõ bất lợi lớn hơn và có đủ ba hướng của mỗi Body. Em dùng 'Firstly/Moreover/Also' để báo ba lợi ích và 'Initially/Subsequently/Furthermore/Last but not least' cho mặt trái; tuy nhiên hai nhánh tiền bạc và thời gian chăm sóc vốn chung một cơ chế bị tách như hai lý do, nên câu chủ đề Body 2 chưa cho thấy rõ ba nhóm chi phí, chuyên môn, xã hội. Mở bài 'face-to-face with their parents' không diễn đạt việc học tại nhà, 'I believed' sai thì, Body 2 còn 'approach do not' và 'one parents'. Em nên chỉnh câu, rồi nhóm lại ba lý do theo đúng quan hệ.

paragraphs: In some countries, children are taught at home by their parents rather than going to school. Personally, I believe that the disadvantages of homeschooling are far more significant than its advantages.

It is argued that homeschooling does have several benefits for both parents and children. Firstly, as no school fees are required, it allows parents to save money and avoid school-related financial pressure. Moreover, when children are educated at home, they are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which can cause emotional and mental disorders. Also, parents can tailor the curriculum and pedagogical approaches while teaching their children at home, which is often not the case in traditional schooling owing to large classes.

However, those advantages of homeschooling come with substantial drawbacks. Initially, this approach may not actually save money, as parents need to pay for lab equipment and tutors; one parent may also need to set aside working time to cater for the child's needs. Furthermore, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts to children and ultimately academic problems. Finally, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, although the merits of homeschooling are noticeable, I am convinced that its demerits are far more significant.
